analysis:
Examined base text of provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/ProviderLoop.swift (lines 1-1192), together with the complete patch (range_map_complete=true).

The only change is in the add-on hold state block (base 493, head 493-502). It reworded a comment and added two stored properties:
- addonHoldSettleTimeout, defaulting to ProviderLoop.addonHoldSettleTimeoutDefault. That constant is defined elsewhere and not supplied.
- addonHoldBeforeCancellingStragglersForTesting, a nil-in-production test hook that suspends the drain bound's cancellation pass.

Both are internal actor state. This file shows no new IPC, wire, crypto or attestation surface. The surrounding addonHolds, addonIPCServer, addonPeerAuthenticatorOverride and addonHoldDrainTimeout are unchanged and relate to TB-012, A-018 and T-059. Under T-059, a same-UID process could try to hold the provider out of routing.

Security relevance depends on how ProviderLoop+AddonHold.swift uses the settle timeout and the straggler-cancellation path. This includes:
- whether a settle bound lets a hold leave the provider out of routing longer than the lease;
- whether models could load beside running VMs;
- whether a release interleaving with straggler cancellation could leave in-flight consumer requests (A-001) cancelled or admission state inconsistent.

Those implementations are not in this batch. The test hook is nil by default, and no production setter is visible here. The integration pass should confirm it cannot be set outside the test module.

No regression is identified from this file alone. The keyPair, signer and attestation initialization are unchanged.
